title: Radiologi Tumor Cerebri
subtitle: Kimi rerun: neuro_radiology
summary: Kuliah radiologi tentang tumor otak yang mencakup karakteristik pencitraan glioma (grade rendah dan tinggi), meningioma, adenoma hipofisis, schwannoma (neuroma akustik), metastasis, dan limfoma. Membahas temuan CT dan MRI termasuk pola penyangatan kontras, karakteristik difusi, fitur spektroskopi, dan diagnosis banding berdasarkan fitur pencitraan. Menyertakan tanda radiologi kunci untuk grading dan lokalisasi tumor.
High-grade gliomas show irregular ring enhancement, central necrosis, surrounding edema, mass effect
Meningioma: extra-axial, broad dural base, homogeneous enhancement, dural tail sign
Acoustic neuroma: CPA mass, extends into internal auditory canal (ice cream cone sign)
exam_focus: Glioblastoma: butterfly appearance, ring enhancement, necrosis
Meningioma: dural tail sign, homogeneous enhancement, extra-axial
Acoustic neuroma: CPA mass, ice cream cone sign
Pituitary adenoma: snowman sign, bitemporal hemianopia
Metastases: multiple, gray-white junction, disproportionate edema
learning_goals: Mengidentifikasi tumor otak umum pada CT dan MRI
Membedakan glioma berdasarkan grade menggunakan fitur pencitraan
Mengenali temuan pencitraan khas meningioma, adenoma hipofisis, dan schwannoma
Menerapkan fitur pencitraan untuk membedakan metastasis dari tumor primer

Pituitary adenoma: sellar mass, may extend suprasellar (snowman sign), cavernous sinus invasion
Metastases: typically multiple, at gray-white junction, disproportionate edema to size

sections.title: Glioma - Grade Rendah dan Tinggi

content.text: GLIOMAS are primary brain tumors arising from glial cells. LOW-GRADE GLIOMA (WHO Grade II): CT shows hypodense or isodense lesion, may have calcification, minimal or no enhancement. MRI T1 shows hypointense, T2/FLAIR shows hyperintense, typically well-defined, minimal surrounding edema, no necrosis. Slow-growing, may transform to high-grade. HIGH-GRADE GLIOMA (WHO Grade III-IV, glioblastoma): CT shows irregular hypodense center (necrosis) with ring-enhancing margins, significant surrounding hypodensity (vasogenic edema), mass effect. MRI T1 shows heterogeneous with ring enhancement, T2/FLAIR shows extensive hyperintense edema beyond tumor margin, central necrosis appears hyperintense on DWI (restricted diffusion in tumor). Glioblastoma shows thick irregular ring enhancement with central necrosis, often crosses corpus callosum (butterfly glioma). Spectroscopy shows elevated choline, reduced NAA, lactate/lipid peak.
Glioblastoma crossing corpus callosum = 'butterfly' appearance; highly characteristic

sections.title: Meningioma dan Adenoma Hipofisis

content.text: MENINGIOMA: Extra-axial tumor from meningothelial cells. CT shows hyperdense (isodense to brain), may have calcification (psammomatous), intense homogeneous enhancement, hyperostosis of adjacent bone. MRI T1 isointense to cortex, intense homogeneous enhancement, dural tail sign (tumor extension along dura), CSF cleft sign (cleavage plane between tumor and brain). PITUITARY ADENOMA: Sellar mass. Microadenoma (<10mm): hypointense on T1 compared to normal pituitary, enhances less than surrounding gland on dynamic contrast (appears as non-enhancing focus). Macroadenoma (>=10mm): expands sella, may extend suprasellar (compressing optic chiasm - bitemporal hemianopia), cavernous sinus invasion (encasing ICA), inferior extension into sphenoid sinus. Snowman sign when suprasellar extension is constricted by diaphragma sellae.
Meningioma: ekstra-aksial, dural tail sign, hiperostosis
Makroadenoma: ekstensi suprasellar (snowman sign), invasi sinus kavernosus
Dural tail sign = dural enhancement extending from tumor margin; classic for meningioma but not pathognomonic

sections.title: Schwannoma dan Metastasis

content.text: SCHWANNOMA (ACOUSTIC NEUROMA/VESTIBULAR SCHWANNOMA): CPA (cerebellopontine angle) mass originating from vestibular nerve. CT shows widening of internal auditory canal (IAC). MRI T1 shows hypointense to isointense, intense enhancement, extends into IAC creating 'ice cream cone' appearance. Larger tumors may compress brainstem and cerebellum, cause hydrocephalus. Cystic components common in larger tumors. METASTASES: Most common brain tumors in adults. Typically multiple lesions at gray-white matter junction. CT shows hypodense (may be hyperdense if hemorrhagic). MRI T1 hypointense with ring or homogeneous enhancement, T2/FLAIR shows disproportionate surrounding edema compared to size of enhancing lesion. Common primary sources: lung, breast, melanoma, kidney, colon. Hemorrhagic metastases: melanoma, renal cell, choriocarcinoma, thyroid, lung.
CPA mass extending into IAC = vestibular schwannoma until proven otherwise

sections.title: Limfoma dan Diagnosis Banding

content.text: PRIMARY CNS LYMPHOMA: Typically B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Immunocompetent: solitary or few periventricular lesions, homogeneous enhancement (disrupted BBB), hyperdense on CT (high cellularity), restricted diffusion on DWI (high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio), extends along ependymal or meningeal surfaces. Immunocompromised (HIV): ring-enhancing lesions, may be indistinguishable from toxoplasmosis; EBV PCR in CSF is diagnostic. DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS APPROACH: Location (intra-axial vs extra-axial), single vs multiple, age, enhancement pattern, associated findings (edema, calcification, hemorrhage, bone changes). Key differentiators: Glioblastoma (ring-enhancing, necrosis, crosses corpus callosum); Abscess (thin smooth ring, restricted diffusion in center); Metastasis (multiple, gray-white junction, known primary); Lymphoma (periventricular, homogeneous enhancement, restricted diffusion).
Limfoma CNS primer: periventrikular, enhancement homogen, restricted diffusion
Limfoma immunokompromai: ring-enhancing, sulit dibedakan dari toksoplasmosis
Diagnosis banding: lokasi, jumlah, pola enhancement
Primary CNS lymphoma: periventricular, homogeneous enhancement, marked restricted diffusion (high cellularity)

Meningioma: extra-axial, dural tail, broad dural base; Schwannoma: CPA, extends into IAC
Lymphoma: periventricular, homogeneous; Toxoplasmosis: multiple, ring-enhancing, basal ganglia
